analysis.title: GS Materials Nov 10: Aramco CEO kicks off Carbonomics today, Gold thoughts, AAL progress, Copper equity pivot GSXGCOPP, FMG's bind grows
key_insights: Asia traders report China demand is 'so so meh'. Hot steel production may decelerate this week, which is negative for iron ore.

Desk view on copper: the physical market is tight but may be at peak tightness. November China imports are in the ~200kt region, with December tracking much lower (~55kt, pre-tariff levels). This holds only if there are no supply issues and no tariff change.
Desk sees apathy in the copper commodity but a different story in copper equities. Investors who hid in commodities can rotate into equities. GSXGCOPP is called 'still a very easy expression'.

AAL moved on diamonds news. Botswana agreed to go to 30% ownership, and the company is working on finalising agreements with Anglo American, plus a 'Global Diamond Consortium' with major customers and the governments of Namibia and Angola.

Gold: GS took its price forecast down to $4,150 per the note. Most investors still rank gold at the top of what they want to own, just not today. The desk calls it an oil trade in which CTAs have the reaction function.

GIR view is that the hiking cycle is 'one and done', with upside risk in March 2027 if energy stays elevated. Next gold data point is central bank buying for October, due Friday 13/11. ETF demand has pulled back, CTAs are short, and open interest is down about 6%.

Barrick (not covered at GS) reported results 'down the middle'. Gold production guided to the low end, copper guidance reiterated despite a Q3 miss, and costs face upward pressure (copper at the high end).

FMG: the Chairman's sale of more than 41m shares appears to be a transfer involving Coaxial, which is Nicola Forrest's vehicle. There is onshore chatter that China may extend the embargo on FMG products. GIR is sell rated on FMG.
Desk sees downside risk to China onshore steel demand, and with it iron ore demand and price.

Copper physical market is 'tight as a drum', with fresh highs daily in China and Yangshan physical premia at fresh all-time highs. China social plus bonded inventory fell 7kt (8%) over the weekend to -73% y/y from -70% y/y on Thursday.
China copper smelter utilisation fell from 81% in October to 61% in November, ahead of CESCO in Shanghai during Thanksgiving week.
Iron ore: Simandou is to reach its full 120m tonne capacity by end-2027 per CTG. The desk says mine decline is the line item the market must consider as a way to balance the market.
Coal is tight and trades against the gas price. The desk is watching the Yunnan water level most closely, described as critical and near winter 2022 levels.

GS hosted a battery corporate day in Shenzhen with 5 producers and 6 materials makers. Discussion covered the consumption tax pass-through, the export VAT rebate phase-out, lower lithium prices, near-term volumes and the 2027 demand and supply outlook.

China extended its suspension of new rare earth controls until January. Canada/China MOU headline suggests the market is looking for TECK approval, with the APEC summit next week as the next catalyst.

China midday wrap: SHCOMP closed about flat, ChiNext +1.49%, GS China Optical Network +3.56%, tech surged as oil fell. Exports missed slightly, imports came in well above estimate, and China's trade surplus topped $1tn for the second time ever.

market_movers.rationale: GIR is sell rated on FMG. The desk sees downside risk to China onshore steel and iron ore demand, and chatter that China may extend the embargo on FMG products.
Anglo American (AAL LN): Botswana agreed to go to 30% in the diamonds process. The desk says the chart trend range looks fine and the CEO was 'very optimistic' at the GS conference.
GSXGCOPP, the GS copper equity basket, is described as 'still a very easy expression' as copper equities diverge from the commodity price.

sector_views.rationale: Desk prefers the equity expression over the commodity, which it sees as apathetic and possibly at peak tightness.
China steel demand is soft, hot steel production may decelerate, and Simandou ramps to 120m tonnes by end-2027.

earnings_insights: Barrick Q3 reported 11/9: EPS 82c reported (VA consensus 83c, BBG consensus 78c). EBITDA $3.46bn reported (consensus $3.34bn VA, $3.42bn BBG).
Barrick Q3 reported 11/9: gold production 816koz (consensus 810koz, Nevada 399koz). Copper production 50kt (consensus 53kt), a miss.
Barrick FY guidance maintained: gold 2.9-3.25moz (consensus 3.18moz). AISC guided at $1,768-1,950/oz against consensus $1,841 and a reported cost of $1,911. Capex guide unchanged at $3.8-4.2bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Second time the surplus has topped $1tn. Exports missed slightly and imports came in well above estimate.
Desk tracking, with December expected much lower at about 55kt, back to pre-tariff levels.
Fell in October despite higher prices. October has one more day than September.
GS took its gold price down to $4,150.
Sharp drop ahead of CESCO in Shanghai.

trade_ideas.description: Long copper equities via the GSXGCOPP basket versus the copper commodity
trade_ideas.rationale: Copper equities diverge from a tight physical market, and investors can rotate from commodities into equities.
trade_ideas.risk: Supply issues or tariff changes could break the view that copper is at peak tightness.

risk_factors: Copper view assumes no supply issues and no tariff change.
China steel demand downside and possible extension of the embargo on FMG products.
Yunnan water levels near winter 2022 lows, affecting power and coal.
Ferrexpo outage after attacks on the Ukraine power grid.
Gold upside risk to the hiking cycle in March 2027 if energy remains elevated.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical market is 'tight as a drum', with fresh highs in China, record Yangshan premia and falling inventories.
tension_points.bear_case: Tightness may be at its peak, with November China imports near 200kt and December tracking about 55kt, and smelter utilisation falling from 81% to 61%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The bear view assumes no supply issues and no tariff. A supply disruption or a tariff change would break it.
